subject: Request: operator runbook & tenant slicing proof for AurumBank RFP
messages:
From: Maya Rosen <maya.rosen@aurumbank.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@aurumbank.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: operator runbook & tenant slicing proof for AurumBank RFP

Hi Alex,

Thanks for taking AurumBank through the initial capabilities call yesterday. As part of our procurement/security review for the RFP, we need a concise package showing how Redwood enforces tenant isolation and the operational controls operators follow during incident scenarios. Specifically we need:

- An operator runbook (step-by-step) that covers tenant isolation, failover, and targeted mitigation for noisy neighbors.
- Network/segmentation diagram that highlights control plane vs runtime demarcation, egress filtering, and any sealed-subnet constructs.
- Evidence artifacts: example audit excerpts (redacted), KV-cache access controls, and a short threat-mitigation matrix for lateral movement.
- Answers to two quick questions: do operators ever execute arbitrary shell commands inside tenant-exposed runtime containers? If so, when and what approvals are recorded?

Target timeline: can you provide these materials by COB Monday (11/22)? We may follow up with a short clarifying call.

Thanks,
Maya Rosen
Sr. Information Security Manager | AurumBank
secops@aurumbank.com

(Attachment: aurumbank-rfp-ask-20261121.pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rosen <maya.rosen@aurumbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator runbook & tenant slicing proof for AurumBank RFP

Maya,

Appreciate the clear list — we can deliver a focused packet by COB Monday. Quick summary up front:

- Operator runbook: attached (operator_runbook_v3.pdf) — covers normal ops, isolation handoffs, and emergency containment.
- Diagram: attached as PNG (network-segmentation-diagram-arn.png). It annotates control plane vs runtime, ingress/egress paths, and our sidecar-based egress filters.
- Evidence: tenant-slicing-evidence.zip contains redacted audit extracts, sample KV ACL entries, and a short CSV of tokenization/access logs for a synthetic tenant used in our internal tests.

Direct answers to your two questions:
1) Operators do not execute arbitrary shell commands in tenant runtime containers. Day-to-day ops rely on admin APIs and CRI-level tooling in the host, not exec into tenant processes.
2) In the rare emergency where process inspection is required (e.g., confirmed malicious process), an operator can perform an exec action via the host-side inspection tool only after approval from our on-call SRE lead and with an automated ticket and audit flag. The runbook section 4.2 documents the approval flow.

Would you like a 30-minute walkthrough Monday AM (we have 09:00–11:00 PT available)?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
(Attachments: operator_runbook_v3.pdf; network-segmentation-diagram-arn.png; tenant-slicing-evidence.zip)
